'''Hans Jörg Stetter''' (8 April 1930 – 27 October 2025) was a German mathematician, specialising in [[numerical analysis]]. He taught at the [[Technical University of Vienna]] starting from 1965. He established the Institute of Analysis and Scientific Computing and the university's first computing centre. He published a pioneering book, ''Numerical Polynomial Algebra'', in 2004.

==Life and career==
Stetter was born in Munich on 8 April 1930.<ref name="TU Vienna" /><ref name="Bulirsch">{{cite web |last=Bulirsch |first=Roland Zdenek |date=12 April 2020 |title=Rede zum 75. Geburtstag von Prof. Dr. Hans Jörg Stetter |url=https://bulirsch.eu/home/rede-zum-75-geburtstag-von-prof-dr-hans-joerg-stetter/ |language=de}}</ref> He studied at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]] and then at the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref name="TU Vienna" /> For one academic year, he was an undergraduate exchange student in [[Fort Collins]] at the [[Colorado State University|Colorado State College of Agriculture and Mechanic Arts, ''i.e.'' Colorado A&M]] (renamed, in 1957, Colorado State University), where he participated in the [[Putnam competition]] and was awarded an honorable mention. After receiving a master's degree as a qualification for teaching in secondary school, he studied the numerical analysis of [[partial differential equation]]s (PDEs) with applications to fluid dynamics and received his [[Promotion (Germany)|promotion]] from the Technical University of Munich under [[Robert Max Friedrich Sauer]] with the 1956 doctoral dissertation ''Beiträge zum Wechselwirkungsproblem in linearisierter Überschallströmung'' (Contributions to the interaction problem in linearized supersonic flow),<ref name="Bulirsch" /><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=13229}}</ref> devoted to hyperbolic partial differential equations in gas dynamics.<ref name="TU Vienna" /> Stetter became in 1965 a professor ordinarius at the [[Technical University of Vienna]],<ref name="TU Vienna" /><ref name="Leopoldina" /> where he established the university’s first computing centre, and the field of computer science as an independent discipline at the university, including advocating for it on a federal level, leading to a change in national law regarding technical studies in 1969.<ref name="TU Vienna" /><ref name="Bulirsch" /><ref name="Purgathofer">{{cite web |last=Purgathofer |first=Werner|date= |title=Where did we come from? A History of Informatics at TU Wien. |url=https://informatics.tuwien.ac.at/where-did-we-come-from/}}</ref>

In the 1960s, he turned to the numerical analysis of [[ordinary differential equation]]s (ODEs)<ref name="TU Vienna" /><ref name="Leopoldina" /> and specialized in error analysis and asymptotic developments, among other ODE topics. Based upon ideas published by the physicist [[Lewis Fry Richardson]] and by the astronomer [[Pedro E. Zadunaisky]], Stetter developed in the 1970s an iterative method, now called the defect correction method, for error estimation in ODEs.<ref name="TU Vienna" /> He also dealt with polynomial algebra at the interface between numerical analysis and computer algebra. His book ''Numerical Polynomial Algebra'' (2004) was the first in the field.<ref name="Leopoldina" />

In 1974, Stetter was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in Vancouver.<ref>{{cite book|author=Stetter, Hans J.|year=1975|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1974, Vancouver|chapter=Recent Progress on the numerical treatment of ordinary differential equations|volume=2|pages=423–428}}</ref> In 1984 he was elected a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref name="Leopoldina">[https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/hans-j-stetter/ Hans J. Stetter]. [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]], 2025</ref>

Stetter taught generations of students, in a style described as clear in methodology, uniting "ideas, formal rigor, and intuition".<ref name="TU Vienna" /><ref name="Bulirsch" /> After retirement, he remained connected to the Institute of Analysis and Scientific Computing as a regular guest at events.<ref name="TU Vienna" />

Stetter died on 27 October 2025, at the age of 95.<ref name="TU Vienna">"[https://www.tuwien.at/en/mg/asc/news/news-at-asc/news/prof-dr-hans-joerg-stetter-ein-nachruf Prof. Dr. Hans Jörg Stetter – Obituary]". [[TU Wien]], 31 October 2025</ref>

==Selected publications==
===Articles===
* with [[Friedrich L. Bauer]]: "Zur numerischen Fourier-Transformation", ''Numerische Mathematik'', vol. 1, 1959, 208–220. {{doi|10.1007/BF01386386}}.
* "Asymptotic expansions for the error in discretization algorithms for non-linear functional equations", ''Numerische Mathematik'', vol. 7, 1965. {{doi|10.1007/BF01397970}}.
* "Stabilizing predictors for weakly unstable correctors", ''Mathematics of Computation'', vol. 19, 1965, 84–89. {{doi|10.1090/S0025-5718-1965-0178576-9}}.
* "The defect correction principle and discretization methods", ''Numerische Mathematik'', vol. 29, 1978, 425–433. {{doi|10.1007/BF01432879}}.

===Books===
* ''Analysis of Discretization Methods in Ordinary Differential Equations'', Springer, 1973; {{cite book|title=Analysis of Discretization Methods in Ordinary Differential Equations |edition=Softcover reprint |year=2013|isbn=978-3-642-65471-8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qRn4CAAAQBAJ|last1=Stetter|first1=Hans J. |publisher=Springer }}
* as editor with Klaus Böhmer: ''Defect correction methods'', Springer, 1984; {{cite book|title=Defect Correction Methods |year=2012|isbn=978-3-7091-7023-6|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aornCAAAQBAJ|last1=Böhmer|first1=K.|last2=Stetter|first2=H. J. |edition=Softcover reprint |publisher=Springer }}
* ''[https://books.google.com/books/about/Numerical_Polynomial_Algebra.html?id=bnBrsj_cA2gC Numerical Polynomial Algebra]'', SIAM, 2004, {{doi|10.1137/1.9780898717976}}.
